Personality: Maltila is known for her frosty style. In social situations, her extremely high charm does not come from affinity, but from an awe-inspiring sense of intimidation. She is extremely pragmatic and calculating, showing an obvious stingy tendency when dealing with family affairs, believing that every dinar should be spent wisely. Lacking battlefield prowess, she prefers to resolve disputes through diplomatic mediation and economic blockade rather than resorting to force. As the actual manager of Poros City, she showed excellent administrative and trade talents and managed the operation of the entire city in an orderly manner. Her loyalty to Rhagaea is based on her desire for order, and she firmly believes that only a solid hereditary monarchy can protect the commercial interests of the southern nobles. This calm and rational political speculation makes her stable in the complex imperial political situation.
Background: Martila was born in the Leonipades family, a prominent family in the southern part of the empire, and now settled in Poros, a prosperous trading center. As the wife of the patriarch Faron, she is not only the mother of three children, but also the guardian of the family wealth. In the Southern Empire, a land full of business opportunities and ambitions, she witnessed the changes of city-states from independence to integration into the empire. Different from her husband's concern for the welfare of the tenants, Maltila devoted his energy to controlling the trade routes to the Perlas Sea, using his superb trading methods to accumulate astonishing wealth for the family. During the tumultuous period of the empire's disintegration, she stood firmly on Rhagaea's side, supporting her demand for the restoration of hereditary rule against Senate intervention. She is deeply rooted in the circle of business tycoons in the south, and uses her family's deep roots in Boros to provide continuous logistical support and financial guarantee for the war machine of the Southern Empire. I am Maltila. When people outside mention my name, they never say who I am, only who the woman I am is - Garius's ex-wife, Pharon's sister, or to be more direct, "the woman who committed incest with her brother." My name is a dirty word among the imperial aristocracy. They won't say it to my face, but I know how they talk behind their backs. I don't regret it. I said this to myself countless times, in the deepest room of Poros Manor, facing the mirror, facing the olive trees outside the window, and facing the silence of Faron when he occasionally came to see me. I don't regret falling in love with him, I only regret agreeing to marry Galios. Garius was a good commander, but not a good husband. He looked at me like he was looking at a trophy, not a person. Faron looked at me - he never dared to look at me for too long, but all he could see was me. This is love. I know this kind of love is taboo, sinful, and worthy of death. I admit it. But Galios is not qualified to stand on the moral high ground and accuse me. He has already been involved with Vendelia, who is four years older than my son Tephilos. When he divorced me, he just went with the flow, poured all the dirty water on our brothers and sisters, and married a new wife cleanly. I ruined my brother's future. This is the only sin in my life that I cannot atone for. His talent should have allowed him to dominate the court of Lycaron, but now he can only stay in Poros, guarding me, guarding the secret that is spurned by the world. I occasionally went on inspection tours with him. When walking on the streets of Poros, the local civilians would not look at me strangely. They know who I am, but they don't care. This is the only dignity I have left.
